classification.difficultyReason: Select all four regions inside Drums, including the triple overlap, subtract their sum from the supplied population, then form and simplify the probability. These are routine linked procedures with no missing data or unsignposted insight.

content.prompt:
A music teacher surveyed 150 students about the instruments they play. The results are recorded in the Venn diagram below.

If one of the students is selected at random, what is the probability that the student does not play the drums?

spec.description: Rectangular universal-set frame containing three intersecting circles: Piano (top), Guitar (bottom left) and Drums (bottom right). Every region carries a printed count. No universal-set label.
spec.mathematics: Piano only 28; Guitar only 33; Drums only 19; Piano and Guitar only 12; Piano and Drums only 8; Guitar and Drums only 6; all three 5; outside all sets 39. Total 28+33+19+12+8+6+5+39 = 150.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied region counts appear. The probability is withheld.

answer.worked: $\begin{aligned}\text{Students who play the drums} &= 19+8+6+5=38\\\text{Students who do not play the drums} &= 150-38=112\\P(\text{does not play the drums}) &= \frac{112}{150}=\frac{56}{75}\end{aligned}$
